description: Required. The key of the key-value pair: what was observed, as a CURIE. On BDC-HM main the base Observation class types this slot as BaseEnum, an empty placeholder, so no CURIE validates against it on the base class; subclasses bind it (MeasurementObservation to MeasurementObservationTypeEnum, SdohObservation to SdohEnum). Class choice: smoking status goes to MeasurementObservation (OMOP:4282779 and OMOP:43054909 are in its enum); education, family income and occupation go to SdohObservation; numeric and lab results go to MeasurementObservation. The Observation concepts in this guide (breastfeeding, menopause status, menstrual bleeding, pregnancy status) are in no observation_type enum yet; their CURIEs are in the Observation Variables table and need a BDC-HM enum addition before output validates.

One of the value_x slots (exactly one is filled). A value from BaseObservationValueEnum, which on HM main is the union of the education, smoking and occupation value sets. Write the BDC-HM value name (CURRENT_SMOKER, NEVER_SMOKED, ...); the OMOP code in each row below is its meaning. Production writes the OMOP code (for example OMOP:45883537 for NEVER_SMOKED) instead of the name: a known production departure pending Anne's decision. The smoking values below are the only values in the enum for the topics in this guide; no menopause, pregnancy or breastfeeding values exist yet. A yes/no menopause item (for example Have you reached menopause?) cannot be written as a menopause-stage value; it gives postmenopausal versus not-postmenopausal only.
Example source variable description: CIGARETTE SMOKING STATUS|SMOKING STATUS|Current smoking status|CIGARETTE SMOKING STATUS

description: Current smoker (OMOP:40766945). Source categories such as current, still smokes, smoker NOS.
Former smoker (OMOP:45883458). Source categories such as past, quit, ex-smoker.
Unknown if ever smoked (OMOP:45885135). Use when the answer cannot tell never from former or current. Do not use it for a yes/no where no means not current.
Value unknown or not reported (the shared UNKNOWN value inherited from the education value set). Production uses it for a missing source value.
One of the value_x slots. Use for a plain yes/no answer, such as currently breastfeeding, currently pregnant or any menstrual periods. True means yes, False means no.
Example source variable description: CURRENTLY BREASTFEEDING|CURRENTLY PREGNANT?|[Menstrual history and pregnancies]. Have you had any menstrual periods during the past 2 years? Q4 [Reproductive History Form, RHXA. Visit 3]

description: One of the value_x slots. Free text, used only when no coded or boolean form fits. Do not use it to avoid mapping a coded value.
One of the value_x slots. A Quantity (value and unit) for a numeric result such as a count. Numeric results belong in MeasurementObservation unless the concept is in this guide.
Optional. The participant age when the observation was made, an integer number of DAYS (BDC-HM unit d). Convert years with years * 365. Production writes it from the visit age variable.
Example source variable description: Age in years at visit based on date of birth and date of visit

description: Optional. The general category of the observation, free text. Not used by the current Observation concepts.
Optional. The method used to generate the result (for example a questionnaire or a scoring system), free text. Fill it when the source states a method; otherwise leave empty.
Optional and repeatable. A Context object (activity, relative_timing, time_duration) for the circumstances of the observation. Not used by the current Observation concepts.
Required. Links the Observation to the Participant.
Example source variable description: De-identified ARIC subject ID|SHARE ID NUMBER|WHI dbGaP Subject ID

description: Optional. Links the Observation to the Visit or exam where it was recorded.
